attributes.body:
In order to mark something as 'except (A)', or 'besides (A)', 以外（いがい） will be used. This construction is a combination of the kanji 以（い） which means 'by means of', and 外（がい） 'outside'. This expression can most accurately be translated as 'with the exception of (A)', or 'everything outside of (A)'.

To use 以外（いがい）, attach it to the thing that you want to highlight as being the 'all inclusive' amount/area.

Fun Fact

以外（いがい） is also regularly used simply as an expression of surprise, when someone sees, hears, or reads something that is 'outside' of what they expected. However, in these cases, the more correct kanji construction is 意外（いがい） 'out of mind'. This is a regular mistake that even native speakers make, so in many cases, either 意外（いがい） or 以外（いがい） would be understandable.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.body: いがい and を除いて both express exclusion, similar to 'other than' or 'with the exception of' in English. Their meanings are very close and often interchangeable. The main difference is that を除いて is more formal and mainly used in writing, while いがい appears in both casual speech and writing. 土日以外毎日働いています and 土日を除いて毎日働いています both mean 'I work every day except Saturday and Sunday.'.

first_relatable.title: いがい
first_relatable.meaning: Except・besides, Other than, With the exception of

second_relatable.title: を除いて
second_relatable.meaning: Except, With the exception of, Unless

attributes.body: Both forms can express the idea of 'other than', but their nuance and usage differ slightly. いがい emphasizes exceptions, like 'except for' or 'other than,' and attaches directly after nouns, e.g. バナナ以外の果物 means 'fruits other than bananas.' In contrast, ほかに highlights the presence of alternatives, takes の when linking to nouns, e.g. バナナの他に 'other than bananas', and can also start a sentence or phrase.

first_relatable.title: いがい
first_relatable.meaning: Except・besides, Other than, With the exception of

second_relatable.title: ほかに(も)・ほか(に)は
second_relatable.meaning: Other, Another, Any other, Anything else, As well as, Besides, In addition

attributes.body: はともかく carries the nuance of setting something aside to focus on the rest. For example, 田中さんはともかく、みんな来ると思う means 'Setting Tanaka aside, I think everyone will come.'. In contrast, いがい emphasizes exclusion, 田中さん以外はみんな来ると思う means 'I think everyone but Tanaka will come.' So, はともかく avoids commenting on Tanaka, while いがい explicitly excludes him.

second_relatable.title: いがい
second_relatable.meaning: Except・besides, Other than, With the exception of

attributes.body: Both forms express exclusion, but with key differences. いがい (often written in kanji as 以外)  attaches directly to nouns, e.g. サッカー以外 'other than soccer'. It's common in both speech and writing. In contrast, をおいてほかに〜ない is much more formal and academic. It's also used almost exclusively to positively highlight something, while いがい carries no such nuance.
